summary: Completed comprehensive testing of anonymous stranger chat app. Backend APIs working correctly, frontend UI excellent with proper dark theme and fonts, but critical Socket.IO connectivity issue preventing real-time chat functionality.

critical_bugs.issue: Socket.IO server not accessible via public URL - Kubernetes ingress not configured for WebSocket connections
critical_bugs.impact: Complete chat functionality failure - users cannot connect or match
critical_bugs.details: Socket.IO works on localhost:8001 but fails on public URL. WebSocket upgrade requests to /socket.io/ not being routed to backend port 8001

working_endpoints.status: Working correctly - returns online users, chats, cities data

integration_issues.issue: Socket.IO client cannot connect to backend due to routing issue
integration_issues.symptoms: Connect button works but no searching state appears, online count stays at 0

ui_working: Dark theme with purple/pink gradients correctly applied
Syne font for headings, DM Sans for body text
Home page layout and navigation working perfectly
City selection and user preferences saving correctly

passed_tests: Socket.IO server working on localhost with full event handling
Frontend UI loading and rendering perfectly
Settings page form functionality and validation
City selection and local storage persistence
User registration and data persistence in localStorage
action_item_for_main_agent: CRITICAL: Configure Kubernetes ingress to route Socket.IO WebSocket connections (/socket.io/*) to backend port 8001. The Socket.IO server is working perfectly locally but not accessible via the public URL due to missing WebSocket routing configuration.
success_percentage: Backend: 75% (APIs working, Socket.IO routing issue), Frontend: 90% (UI perfect, integration blocked by backend routing)
